html:
Short war in 1890 between France and the West African kingdom of Dahomey, fought around the coastal town of Cotonou, in what is now Benin.

France held trading rights at Cotonou under an 1868 treaty and claimed a protectorate over nearby Porto-Novo. King behanzin of Dahomey rejected both. His army, which included the women soldiers known as the Amazons, attacked Porto-Novo and then Cotonou in early 1890. French troops, with modern rifles and artillery, held the town.

A treaty in October 1890 let France keep Cotonou, and Dahomey was to receive a yearly payment. Neither side trusted it. Dahomey kept buying arms, and in 1892 the Second Franco-Dahomean War began. By 1894 Behanzin was beaten and Dahomey became part of French West Africa.

The war was one step in the European takeover of the African coast after the Berlin Conference and the end of the atlantic-slave-trade, which had made Dahomey rich.
sum: Short war in 1890 between France and the West African kingdom of Dahomey, fought around the coastal town of Cotonou, in what is now Benin.
